Summary: Exodus 20:2 opens the Ten Words with God's self-declaration: 'I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.' In the traditional enumeration this verse is counted as a positive command — the first mitzvah — even though it reads as a statement rather than an imperative, because it grounds every command that follows in who God is.
Commandment: Believe that God exists, and that he is the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt.
Application: Every other command rests on this one: obedience follows from knowing who commands. The New Testament carries the same ground forward — without faith it is impossible to please God, for he that cometh to God must believe that he is (Hebrews 11:6).
Purpose: Scripture's stated ground is the Exodus itself: the God who redeemed Israel is the God who commands Israel (Exodus 20:2).
